summary: MHT-CET engineering college predictor web app; CSV upload/import is being refined and predictor logic will rely on closing_rank only (percentile kept as text/not used in calculations).
architectural_notes: Use SQLite initially for structured storage of cutoff data extracted from CAP PDFs.
Cutoff records stored with fields: year, round, college_name, branch_name, seat_type, category, gender, closing_rank, percentile.
Parse combined cutoff codes (e.g., GOPENH) into gender/category/seat_type attributes.
Prediction compares user estimated rank vs Round 4 closing ranks using thresholds: ≤0.8×cutoff Safe, ≤cutoff Probable, ≤1.2×cutoff Dream.
Frontend-first milestone: build UI without backend/logic initially.
Add a minimal predictor function that maps percentile -> estimated rank using a simple placeholder heuristic (until real data/rank model is implemented).
Expose a lightweight backend endpoint (or server function) that returns dummy results in the format: College | Branch | Chance, to make the form submission functional end-to-end.

User requested real cutoff data support via a `cutoffs` database table (columns: college_name, branch_name, category, gender, seat_type, closing_rank, percentile); implementation to proceed in smaller steps starting with creating the table only.
Treat `percentile` as non-numeric text (or ignore it) during CSV import; do not use it in calculations.
Prediction logic should use only `closing_rank` (not percentile) when classifying Safe/Probable/Dream.
known_issues: Percentile input validation needs to allow decimal values; before rank calculation, percentile should be truncated/floored to an integer (e.g., 90.6 → 90) and then use rank = (100 - integer_percentile) * 2000.

existing_features.title: Create a mobile-friendly frontend page that renders a simple MHT-CET college predictor form with these fields and labels: CET Percentile (number input), Category (dropdown: OPEN, OBC, SC, ST, EWS), Gender (dropdown: Male, Female), Candidature (dropdown: Maharashtra, All India), Home University (dropdown containing major Maharashtra universities), TFWS (yes/no), and a Submit button.

Implement basic client-side form state wiring purely for UI purposes (no predictor logic and no backend calls): inputs should be editable, selections should persist in the UI, and submitting should prevent full page reload.

Apply a coherent visual theme across the form (colors, typography, spacing, and components) that feels like an education/exam utility and is consistently used throughout the page; avoid blue/purple as the primary palette.

Wire the existing `frontend/src/pages/MhtCetPredictorFormPage.tsx` submit action to call the backend predictor method using the existing `useActor` hook, and render the returned results in the UI after submission.

Ensure the frontend can call the new backend method by updating the generated frontend backend bindings/types (the `backendInterface` used by `frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts`) to include the predictor method signature and response types.

Add a CSV upload UI to the existing predictor page (`frontend/src/pages/MhtCetPredictorFormPage.tsx`) that lets a user select a `.csv` file, uploads it to the backend import method, and displays the import summary (inserted count and any errors).

Update the generated frontend backend bindings/types (the module imported as `@/backend` and the `backendInterface` used by `frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts`) to include the new CSV import method and any associated response types so TypeScript compilation succeeds.

Update the generated frontend backend bindings/types (the module imported as `@/backend` and the `backendInterface` used by `frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts`) to reflect the updated backend types/signatures resulting from treating `percentile` as text or removing it, so TypeScript compilation succeeds and CSV import + cutoff inspection calls remain type-correct.

Update the backend prediction response type used by `predictAdmission` so each returned row contains exactly the fields needed for the requested table: college name, branch, and closing rank. Align field names and types between Motoko and the generated frontend TypeScript types so the frontend can render without type errors.

Update `frontend/src/pages/MhtCetPredictorFormPage.tsx` so that on successful prediction it displays results in a table with columns: College name, Branch, Closing rank, populated from the backend response. Remove/disable any UI elements that assume a `chance` field for prediction results (e.g., chance badge/coloring) so the rendered results match the requested columns.

Make the frontend’s estimated-rank calculation consistent with the required formula `rank = (100 - percentile) * 2000` wherever the estimated rank is computed/shown in `frontend/src/pages/MhtCetPredictorFormPage.tsx` (so the displayed rank matches the logic used for filtering).

Update the generated frontend backend bindings/types (the module imported as `@/backend`) so it reflects the updated `predictAdmission` return type and any renamed/added/removed fields, without modifying immutable hook sources (do not edit `frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts`).

Update `frontend/src/pages/MhtCetPredictorFormPage.tsx` so the displayed estimated rank uses the same truncation rule as the backend: parse the percentile as a number, truncate to an integer (e.g., 60.56 → 60), then compute `rank = (100 - integer_percentile) * 2000`. Keep allowing decimal entry in the percentile input.

Update the CET Percentile input on `frontend/src/pages/MhtCetPredictorFormPage.tsx` so users can enter decimal percentile values (e.g., 90.6) without the UI rejecting, stripping, or forcing integer-only entry.

Update the CET Percentile field in `frontend/src/pages/MhtCetPredictorFormPage.tsx` to use an HTML numeric input that supports decimals by setting `type="number"`, `step={0.01}`, `min={0}`, and `max={100}`.
Update the browser document title to exactly "MHT-CET College Predictor v2" by changing the <title> in `frontend/index.html`.
Update the visible app header title text in `frontend/src/pages/MhtCetPredictorFormPage.tsx` to exactly "MHT-CET College Predictor v2" (currently rendered as "MHT-CET College Predictor").

new_feature_requests.summary: Build a simple mobile-friendly frontend form UI for MHT-CET college predictor (percentile, category, gender, candidature, home university, TFWS) with submit button; no backend/logic yet
Ingest/upload CAP Round 1–4 cutoff PDFs (Maharashtra + All India seats) and extract cutoff tables into structured data
Create SQLite database schema/table for cutoffs (year, round, college, branch, seat_type, category, gender, closing_rank, percentile) including parsing codes like GOPENH
Implement predictor logic: percentile->estimated rank, filter relevant cutoffs, compare to Round 4 closing ranks, classify Safe/Probable/Dream with thresholds
Create results page/table showing college, branch, cutoff percentile, and chance with color coding (Safe green, Probable orange, Dream red)
Prepare the app for deployment as a simple web app

Add simple backend predictor logic for the existing form: convert percentile to estimated rank (placeholder), return dummy/sample college+branch+chance results, and wire it to the UI so submission shows results

Implement a backend predictor method in `backend/main.mo` that accepts the user’s percentile input, converts it to an estimated rank, and returns dummy/sample prediction results with fields `college`, `branch`, and `chance` (values like Dream/Probable/Safe).

Add a new persistent backend data structure representing a `cutoffs` table with the following columns: `college_name`, `branch_name`, `category`, `gender`, `seat_type`, `closing_rank`, `percentile`. Implement this as a Motoko type plus stable storage in `backend/main.mo` so cutoff records persist across canister upgrades.

Expose minimal backend methods to verify and access the stored cutoff data without requiring CSV upload yet: (1) a query method that returns the total count of cutoff records, and (2) a query method that returns a bounded list (e.g., with start/limit parameters) of cutoff records for inspection/testing.
Add CSV upload support to import cutoff records into the backend `cutoffs` table (validate/parse rows and persist them)

Implement a backend CSV import method that accepts cutoff records as CSV text, validates/parses each row into `CutoffsRecord`, persists the imported records in the backend cutoffs store, and returns an import summary (e.g., total rows processed, rows inserted, and row-level validation errors).
Make the backend cutoffs data persist across canister upgrades so that records imported via CSV remain available after redeploy/upgrade.
Update CSV import and predictor logic so percentile is not parsed as float (store as text or ignore) and use only closing_rank for prediction calculations

Update the backend cutoff record model so that the `percentile` column is not parsed as a Float during CSV import (store it as plain text or otherwise exclude it from numeric parsing), and ensure `closing_rank` remains the only numeric field used for prediction calculations.

Update the backend CSV parsing/import logic in `backend/main.mo` to parse `closing_rank` from CSV text using a supported numeric parser (e.g., `Nat.fromText`), and remove the current placeholder float parsing/trap path for both `closing_rank` and `percentile`. Also harden parsing to handle common CSV line endings and whitespace (e.g., CRLF).

Update backend prediction logic so that any comparisons against historical cutoff data use only `closing_rank` (do not use cutoff `percentile` values in calculations). If prediction logic currently does not use stored cutoffs, ensure that any future-facing or placeholder logic does not reference cutoff percentile numerically and that the code path is consistent with “closing_rank-only” evaluation.

Implement actual predictor logic on "Predict My Colleges": convert percentile to estimated rank via rank=(100-percentile)*2000, compare against uploaded CSV cutoffs using closing_rank, and display a results table (College name, Branch, Closing rank) including only rows where rank <= closing_rank

Implement actual backend prediction in `backend/main.mo` for `predictAdmission(userPercentile: Text)` by: (1) parsing `userPercentile` as a number in the range 0–100, (2) converting it to an estimated rank using `rank = (100 - percentile) * 2000`, and (3) filtering the imported cutoff records so that a cutoff is included in results when `rank <= closing_rank`. The method must no longer `trap` as a placeholder when valid input is provided.
Allow decimal percentile inputs; truncate percentile to an integer (e.g., 60.56 -> 60) before rank calculation and use rank=(100-integer_percentile)*2000

Update backend `predictAdmission(userPercentile: Text)` in `backend/main.mo` to accept decimal percentile strings (e.g., `"60.56"`), truncate the parsed percentile to an integer (e.g., 60.56 → 60), and use the updated prediction formula `rank = (100 - integer_percentile) * 2000` for filtering cutoff records.
Update CET Percentile input to be type=number with step=0.01, min=0, max=100 to allow decimal percentile entry
Update the app title to "MHT-CET College Predictor v2" (UI/document title/branding as applicable)
